purpose: Alternative-source evidence for five GrowFit foods still awaiting micronutrient matching. This file is research documentation only; it is not consumed by the current enrichment script and does not modify the food bank.

rules: Do not treat a study value as a per-100g edible-portion value unless its basis is explicitly reported.
Keep dry-weight, wet-weight, cooked, raw, and unclear-basis observations distinct.
Record nutrient-specific provenance; never assign one source to nutrients it did not measure.
Do not map toxic contaminants such as lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury, or aluminium into nutritional mineral fields.
Do not convert salt to sodium without a clearly documented method and matching product basis.
Missing or uncertain values remain null.

evidence.title: The Nutrient Content of South African Lamb & Mutton
evidence.foodIdentity: Cooked lean edible portion; subcutaneous fat removed; shoulder, loin and leg reported separately
evidence.sampleAndMethod: 18 lamb carcasses per age group; Dorper and Merino from three production regions; cuts cooked at 160 C to 70 C internal temperature. Minerals by ICP-OES; vitamins by specified AOAC/Wilmalasiri methods.
evidence.basis: per 100 g cooked lean edible portion
qualityNotes: The source is South African and the animal breeds and production regions differ from an unspecified Iranian lamb product.
The leg cut was cooked by dry heat; shoulder used moist heat.
The source warns that iron, zinc and B-vitamin analytical methods may have been inconsistent and says values require scrutiny.
The lamb-leg macro profile (about 171 kcal, 25.4 g protein, 7.67 g fat per 100 g) differs substantially from GrowFit's current base macros (250 kcal, 26 g protein, 16 g fat).
The food-bank label does not specify cut, visible-fat removal level, or cooking method.
evidence.reason: Useful as a transparent comparison source, but not a defensible exact match for the current GrowFit food definition.

foods.nextEvidenceNeeded: Define the cut, whether intermuscular fat is included, and the cooking method; then search a national composition table or laboratory study matching that definition.

evidence.title: Salt Contents in Fermented Dairy Products: A Strategic Blueprint for Healthier Intake
evidence.basis: sample salt and moisture; not a complete micronutrient panel
qualityNotes: The study reports salt and moisture, not calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, zinc or vitamins.
Salt is not interchangeable with sodium in the GrowFit schema; no sodium conversion is made here.

evidence.title: Microbial and Chemical Characteristics of Doogh (Iranian Fermented Milk Drink)
evidence.foodIdentity: Commercial and traditional yoghurt drink samples; 148 samples in the survey
qualityNotes: The article explains that recipes vary in yoghurt, water and salt proportions.
Its main survey measures salt, preservatives and microbiological indicators; it does not provide the complete per-100g micronutrient profile required by GrowFit.

evidence.title: Iranian Food Composition Table
qualityNotes: FAO identifies the National Nutrition and Food Technology Research Institute's 2017 Iranian Food Composition Table and points to EuroFIR FoodEXplorer.
The database is listed as restricted access; item-level Doogh records could not be independently retrieved in this review.

foods.nextEvidenceNeeded: Obtain a directly accessible Iranian Food Composition Table record or a laboratory study measuring the same style of doogh and reporting nutrient values per 100 g or 100 mL.

evidence.title: Dephytinisation of Sangak and Barbari bread made from different extraction rate flours increases iron and zinc bioaccessibility in Caco-2 cells
evidence.basis: reported as micrograms per gram; moisture basis not confirmed in the accessible record
qualityNotes: The paper compares Sangak and Barbari and reports mineral and phytate values.
The indexed table does not establish a compatible wet-weight edible-portion basis for direct insertion into GrowFit.
Only four minerals are reported in the accessible table; this is not a complete micronutrient profile.

evidence.title: Determination of Zinc Contents in Iranian Flat Breads
evidence.sampleAndMethod: 36 flat-bread samples overall, collected in Tehran in 2004; zinc measured by flame atomic absorption spectrophotometry.
evidence.basis: mg/kg; moisture basis not specified in the accessible abstract
qualityNotes: The study is older and reports zinc only.
It does not provide a full nutrient panel or an explicit moisture basis.

foods.nextEvidenceNeeded: Find a direct Sangak food-composition analysis that states wet-weight basis, moisture, sample count, flour extraction rate and a broader set of minerals/vitamins.

evidence.title: Dephytinisation of Sangak and Barbari bread made from different extraction rate flours increases iron and zinc bioaccessibility in Caco-2 cells
evidence.basis: reported as micrograms per gram; moisture basis not confirmed in the accessible record
qualityNotes: Only four minerals are reported in the accessible table.
The paper describes extraction-rate flour differences and bioaccessibility; the values are not a complete per-100g wet-weight profile.

evidence.title: Determination of metal(oids) in different traditional flat breads distributed in Isfahan city, Iran
evidence.sampleAndMethod: Fresh daily-baked samples collected from 31 separate bakeries. Samples oven-dried at 50 C for 48 hours; mineralized by acid digestion; elements measured by ICP-OES and selected contaminants by AAS.
qualityNotes: The published basis is dry weight because samples were oven-dried before analysis.
These values cannot be converted to per-100g as-eaten bread without a matching moisture value.
The study also measures toxic elements; those are not nutritional fields and are excluded from this record.
The study notes that flour type, bran extraction, salt and bakery processes can change element levels.

crossFoodSources.title: Iranian Food Composition Table
crossFoodSources.note: FAO lists the National Nutrition and Food Technology Research Institute's 2017 table, but access is restricted through EuroFIR FoodEXplorer.

crossFoodSources.title: FAO/INFOODS Guidelines for Food Matching
crossFoodSources.note: Use the closest food identity and preparation-state match available, document the selected match, and record limitations when an exact match is unavailable.

overallConclusion.reason: The alternative sources improve the evidence trail, but none currently supplies a complete, directly comparable micronutrient panel on the food bank's required per-100g edible-portion basis for the exact food definition.
overallConclusion.recommendedNextStep: Review the evidence with the food-bank schema owner, then design nutrient-level provenance support before any non-USDA values are considered for import.
